chunks: And what occurred between Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), and their arbitration by the Hajar (Black Stone), is well-known; we shall not prolong [the text] by mentioning it here.

key_terms.إِلَى الْحَجَرِ: To the Stone (referring to the Black Stone)

ai.seo_question: What is the incident of arbitration between Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya and Imam Sajjad involving the Black Stone?
ai.summary: This passage from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* references the well-known arbitration (*hukm*) between Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya and Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) regarding the Black Stone, a key event in the Khawarij controversy. By noting its familiarity, Tusi signals that this incident serves as a foundational proof for the Kaisaniyya sect's claim to leadership, which he subsequently refutes in the chapter. The brevity here underscores the scholarly convention of assuming the reader's prior knowledge of this pivotal historical dispute.
